# BOOK 1 OF 2: SHOULDER TO SHOULDER (Gordon Stables, Gutenberg 76046)

**Dedication:** To Dr. John Robertson, from his cousin the author. Epigraph from Burns ("Be Britain still to Britain true...").
**Frontispiece:** "Hurrah, my lads; remember Egypt!" shouted Sir John Moore (p. 310).

**Structure:** Book I "In the Highlands a Hundred Years Ago" (Ch I–XI); Book II "Off to Join his Regiment" (Ch I–VIII); Book III "From War to Gentle Peace" (Ch I–XIV).

## Narrator and frame
- Narrator "Williamie" (author), a small boy, sits on a creepie (low stool) by his grandfather's knee, listening to tales in winter forenights. Grandfather = "Auld-da", a Highland soldier (ex-1st Royal Scots, "Pontius Pilate's Guards"), lived in a but-and-ben cottage near Ury (Inverurie), died aged ~89 ("Mercy! Mercy!"). Grandfather read only the Bible and *Looking unto Jesus*. Walked to Aberdeen each quarter day for half-pay, twirling a stick; gave narrator and sister Sissie half-crowns and apples/nuts. Narrator later says he wrote this "in a wigwam", thirty years after grandfather's death.
- Narrator's family: father (Gordon), mother; narrator is a Gordon through father, Robertson through mother's side (Braes of R----, Robertsons of Struan origin).
- Grandfather's claymore trick: circles sword near door-edge without touching door or nose.

## BOOK I (Highlands, 1745 onward)
**Ch I – Auld-da.** Grandfather's life stories told by fireside.

**Ch II – My Hero, Bonnie Prince Charlie.** Narrator, age 7, a Jacobite at heart; mother sang songs ("He's owre the hills", "Cam' ye by Athol", "O, wae's me for Prince Charlie"). Narrator condemns "bloody Duke of Cumberland" who shot a wounded Highlander after an English officer refused ("Your Grace, I am your humble servant, but not your executioner"). Grandfather forbids Pretender talk: his father's kin were rebels, mother's Robertsons royalists. Grandfather's regiment was Royal Scots; Duke of Kent was his colonel; he once spoke with the Queen as a baby and Duke of Kent saved his life. Song: "O, but you've been long o' coming... royal-welcome Charlie."

**Ch III – First Act in a Tragedy.** Setting: Braes of R----, near Beauly; Ben Wyvis; Belladrum (Lovat castle). Great-grandfather lived to 101, found dead against pine with snuff-box. Fiona Stuart (18, dark-brown eyes, raven tresses; called "Gipsy") is the younger sister of grandmother-to-be, living with the Robertsons. Her sweetheart: Ian Robertson (soldier in the 1st). Raoul McIvor, "Raoul Dhu" / "Black Ronald", Lovat's musician and reveller, tall, handsome, woos Fiona. Scene: Fiona with deerhound; Raoul offers dog; Fiona refuses. Hare shot by Raoul dies in Fiona's arms; collie named (unnamed) comforts her. Raoul demands she marry him; she says her heart is with Ian ("ma ghaol ma chree"). Raoul threatens to dirk Ian; grabs Fiona's arm. Muirachie, the dwarf (Gaelic-accented English, "ta", "pe"), leaps on Raoul's back and chokes him; Raoul falls; Muirachie says "no pe deaded when ta dew falls."

**Ch IV – Fontenoy, Culloden, the Cave, a Race for Life.** Fontenoy (1745) account: Cumberland attacked; Dutch cowards; Saxe. Grandfather's rebuke of Raoul: Robertson refuses to join Prince Charlie ("I'll follow no cross save that which our Saviour carried"); threatens to stretch Raoul dead. Muirachie warns of Raoul's threat. Winter: Robertson fortifies farm; ten men including Muirachie. After Culloden, Raoul returns to Beauly drunk, vows revenge; Muirachie spies. Robertson's family (wife Mary, children, sister-in-law Fiona) hidden by Muirachie in Corney's Cave (old whisky-still, Beauly). Fiona, wrapped in Highland plaid, Tam-o'-Shanter bonnet, crook, runs fourteen miles to Culloden camp; gives water to dying soldier in her inverted bonnet; meets rebel group; sentry; a camp-fire ambush; she fights pursuer with claymore and wounds him. Reaches Captain McDonald's tent; Ian is writing there; "What, Fiona!" Orders "To horse!" thirty men.

**Ch V – Royals to the Rescue.** Thirty-three riders with Fiona as guide. At Farm: Raoul's attack (fifty men), palisade, battering-ram, fire in copse. Muirachie leads family out of cave; he dies later trying to save cattle. Robertson fights with dirk in last trench; "God help my wife and bairns." Red-coats arrive: "The red-coats are coming!" Ian and Raoul duel; Ian's sword pierces Raoul. Fiona begs mercy; Ian spares him. Raoul taken prisoner, later executed at Edinburgh. Ian and Fiona marry; grandfather born decades later (narrator's grandfather = Ian/John Robertson, son of this couple). Farm burned.

**Ch VI – A Highland School a Hundred Years Ago.** Narrator's Miss Steelyard anecdote (old maid, "boys are monkeys"; egg with chick). Grandfather born ~35 years after events; mother's nurse Yonish MacPhee saw omens (four magpies, deer, raven, sour cream). School run by Dominie Freeschal ("Mister Freeschal"); tawse (leather strap); stone-built school with green glass windows. Ian first day: says "Sir John Robertson is my name..." verse; tawsed. Ian draws caricatures; dominie's tawse-throwing skill.

**Ch VII – Hard Times for a Teacher.** Dominie's wife (Mrs. Freeschal, large), daughter Rachel (age 8, fair hair, blue eyes). Pupils: Tonal (Tonal/"Tonal" spelled "Tonal"), Johnnie Nairn (his mother Mrs. Nairn beat dominie with broom-handle), Sandy Young's complaint. Spelling "believe/deceive/relieve." Rachel's crush; Ian's fights; Kenneth McRae. Ian locked in schoolroom as punishment; key left in door; Rachel feeds him sugar-bools and brandy-snaps through broken pane. Ian climbs chimney to escape, sticks fast, frees himself. Dominie, drunk, meets black-smeared Ian, faints.

**Ch VIII – The Conspirators.** Tonal and Ian burn the tawse in forest. Tonal to enlist. Ian's cock-fight king of school (Yule); dance with Rachel (Reel of Tulloch); Tom Grahame's threat. Ian and Tom fight in forest; Ian's kilt-pin (nicknamed "Preen Mhor") pierces Tom's chest; Tom confined a month. Dominie visits Robertson's farm; Ian leaves school. Rachel's sad farewell at peat-stack.

**Ch IX – Leaving Home; a Humble Trade.** Ian (15) leaves with 5 shillings; to Inverness; staymaker Mr. Craig (High Street; wife, cat) — rats under counter. Cousin Fraser of Falkirk Lodge (Captain of Black Watch) enlists him; Fraser's wife Mrs. Fraser (kind); butler; Donald; servants. Dash the collie. Ian: "I will not serve under a Fraser of Lovat... I am a Robertson and a loyalist."

**Ch X – The King's Shilling.** Ian throws shilling into sea; Dash. Fisherman and daughter at Beauly. Ian goes home; Rachel sends word. Corney's Cave outlaw life; sergeant and soldiers; Ellen (inn girl at Beauly) helps him escape after drugging soldiers with whisky (muskets rammed up chimney, faces blackened). Captured, escapes at 2am.

**Ch XI – Sworn to Shoot at Sight.** Dominie's letter; Chisholm (lawyer, Inverness). Rachel's note with four-bladed clover. Enlists at Fort George with 1st Royals; recruiting sergeant; Ian renamed "John" ("We'll call you John").

## BOOK II (Off to Join His Regiment)
**Ch I** – Drill; Sergeant Brown; Captain Drake (strong fist; "Don't soil your gloves"). Fight between McGruer and Playfair (Pope nose). Packet ship *Vengeful* sails from Inverness in December. Lady Jane at New Year fête.

**Ch II** – Storm; cattle and sheep thrown overboard; sailor lost. Arrive Leith; Edinburgh Castle.

**Ch III** – Captain Drake's hornpipe bet; John dances eleven steps on dinner-table with fife. Dr. McLeod (giant) lifts him. Blood (small lieutenant, wears stays) and McLeod duel quarrel over Miss Niven; McLeod throws Blood out window. O'Reilly vs Drake duel; Blood wounded, bullet hit his stays busk.

**Ch IV** – Drake's account of Revolution, Paris, Danton, Terror, Dumouriez; war with France 1793.

**Ch V** – Toulon, Lord Hood, Napoleon's artillery; Corsica (Bastia, Calvi, Morello); Drake captured by brigands (Corsica), stripped; Calvi storming.

**Ch VI** – John promoted corporal, then sergeant. Drunk Freemason escapade; Colonel W—'s servant; saved by ribbon. Quiberon; Napoleon in Italy (Lodi).

**Ch VII** – Napoleon's ambitions; Ireland rebellion 1798 (Humbert, Castlebar); Flotilla attempt at Sallenelle/Cherbourg.

**Ch VIII** – Furlough 1801; Craig gone; Ellen tells of Rachel's death. Battle of Alexandria (March 21, 1801): Drake wounded (fell but unhurt), Tom Grahame in 42nd; Sir John Moore; Captain Fraser (cousin) dying; daughter Ailie; "Shoulder to shoulder."

## BOOK III (From War to Gentle Peace)
**Ch I** – Ramsgate; Duke of Kent (father of Queen Victoria) takes command of Royals; flea incident; gull shot by O'Reilly; malingerers; mutineer flogged; Tonal the piper; "Miller o' Drone."

**Ch II** – Gibraltar; Duke of Kent is "best-hated man on the Rock"; vendetta stabbing; Drake; Spaniards.

**Ch III** – Mysterious box (mate Myers); meeting of conspirators (Mr. Milan, a masked figure); mutiny Dec 24.

**Ch IV** – Dying soldier forgives Duke; Christmas mutiny 26th; Reilly shot. War renewed 1803. Duke of Enghien murdered; Villeneuve; Nelson race.

**Ch V** – Trafalgar; Blood and Jones killed in skirmish (Blood dies, Jones loses leg); Drake offers recruiting at Dundalk; John meets Mrs. Stapleton and Eleanor (Nora) at Booterstown.

**Ch VI** – Dundalk fair; recruits; schooner *St. Patrick*; Copenhagen bombardment; marriage to Eleanor (Nora), Presbyterian; Killarney.

**Ch VII** – Peninsular War; Junot; Napoleon in Spain; Sir John Moore.

**Ch VIII** – Retreat to Corunna; Tom's orphan baby Annie; Tonal's wound (bagpipes shot through).

**Ch IX** – Corunna (Jan 16, 1809): Moore dies; "Remember Egypt!"; burial lines. Tonal marries Spanish girl, gets new bagpipes at Dover.

**Ch X** – Nora follows John; Saragossa; Bergen-op-Zoom (1814); Robert Robertson born on battlefield; Nora shoots murderous woman.

**Ch XI** – Atlantic voyage in *Salamanca*; barefoot squad inspection; shipwreck at Anticosti; Canadian war (York, Chippewa).

**Ch XII** – Red-Eye (Micmac), Mary (narrator's mother, "daughter of the regiment"); bear episode; Tonal and Mary captured.

**Ch XIII** – Red-Eye's grief; McLeod's oath; moonlit pursuit.

**Ch XIV** – Fight; Red-Eye dies saving Mary; "Lead me through the darkness"; grave; Waterloo missed; Napoleon at St. Helena; ends "Heigho!"

# BOOK 2 OF 2: WILLOW THE KING (J. C. Snaith, Gutenberg 73075)

**Subtitle:** The Story of a Cricket Match. Illustrated by Lucien Davis. Dedication: to colleagues of Nottingham Forest Amateur Cricket Club.

**Chapters:** I Night Before; II Coming Events; III Little Clumpton v. Hickory; IV Impossible Incident; V Cussedness of Cricket; VI Young Person in Brown Holland; VII Conversational; VIII Cricket Lunch; IX Record Breaking; X End of the Day; XI Cupid Puts His Pads On; XII My First County Match; XIII Case of Heredity; XIV Sinned Against; XV Facing the Music; XVI Telegram from Stoddart; XVII Consequences; XVIII Instruction; XIX Case for M.C.C.; XX Case for Another Eminent Authority; Epilogue (Morning Post marriage notice).

**Narrator:** Dimsdale (R. C. "Dimmy", Richard Cranford Dimsdale), young batsman, son of late soap-boiler (Dimsdale's Dirt Defier); servant William (valet); his home at Little Clumpton. Friends: the Optimist (J. Brightside, "Cheery"), the Pessimist (Grimston), the Humourist (Merryweather, "Jessop"), the Worry (Daunton, pro), the Secretary (Lawson, "Notts"), the Captain (Halliday, H. J.), the Treasurer, the Ancient (J. F. S. Oldknow), the General Nuisance (Hon. John Blenkinsop-Comfort), Carteret (fat short-slip, barrister), Lennox, Charlie Trentham (H. C., best bowler, sensation), Archie (A. H., Middlesex, going out with Stoddart), T. S. M. "Tommy" (Harrow captain, youngest), George (Captain, Artillery), Toddles (Rev. E. J. H. Elphinstone, curate), Laura Mary "Grace" Trentham (twin of Tommy; scorer; brown holland; Zingari tie), the Rector (Hon. George Trentham, D.D., ex-bowler, Lord/"Dicky"), Biffin (umpire, ground-man), Wiggles (ground-man), Jennings (butler), Augustus (footman), Jane (maid), Mrs. Jennings, William, Mary (narrator's sister), Ricky (narrator's nickname).

**Ch I** – Night before: team in billiard room; Captain's pipe; Secretary; General Nuisance brings Trenthams news (Hickory with Trentham brothers, Carteret, Elphinstone, Fry).

**Ch II** – William finds cap missing (Authentics). Narrator walks to ground; Wiggles on wicket; Sportsman newspaper reading (A. H. Trentham 97, H. C. 9 wickets, T. S. M. 205). General Nuisance delivers papers; says Billy drunk (ruined; slow bowler). William rides to Thornhill's for lent Authentics.

**Ch III** – Grace arrives in four-in-hand coach driving; scolds Wiggles; orders field; hits narrator's leg? (Grace catches ball; Charlie's arm over screen). Narrator and the Ancient practice.

**Ch IV** – Team arrival; Halliday and Trentham toss dispute ("two wicket-keepers"); Captain Halliday wins toss; narrator opens with Halliday.

**Ch V** – Narrator faces H. C.'s bowling; first over; narrator scores runs; caught leg-before (l.b.w.) by T. S. M. (scores 7).

**Ch VI** – Narrator bored in pavilion; Optimist brings him to Grace on coach; Grace praises his batting; criticises Toddles' drop.

**Ch VII** – Grace's conversation; Ancient's record; "Charlie's arm" tirade.

**Ch VIII** – Lunch on coach roof; champagne; toasts (Stoddart, Archie, Charlie); Charlie's embarrassment; Stoddart letter joke "Name inadvertently omitted"; Rector and Earl arrive; Grace leaves.

**Ch IX** – Halliday 204, reaches first Little Clumpton v Hickory record; Oldknow 101; Merryweather 28; Comfort 59. Grace's Records.

**Ch X** – Partnership record 301 (Barclay & Perkins beaten); declaration not made; Oldknow run out; close 518/4.

**Ch XI** – Narrator's insomnia; General Nuisance mocks him; sister Mary returns; narrator confesses infatuation.

**Ch XII** – Grace on Hickory Rectory lawn, single-wicket game (Archie, George, T. S. M., H. C., Carteret); narrator asked to play Gloucestershire; Grace captains Gloucestershire; library window; Rectory rules; cucumber frame dispute; Toddles' oath; tea; Rector's tobacco plants destroyed by cricket ball.

**Ch XIII** – Heredity of curl; T. S. M. selected for Kent (Tonbridge, Monday; telegram from A. J. Webbe); Grace gets Charlie selection hope; Gloucestershire wins by one wicket.

**Ch XIV** – Bath-room; dinner; Grace hostess; narrator decides to propose.

**Ch XV** – Narrator proposes in library amid averages; Grace ignores him; telegrams; "Will you be my wife?" repeatedly ignored; Augustus interrupts.

**Ch XVI** – Telegram: "If Hawke wants you for India, sing slow. You are going with me. Stoddart." Grace excited; narrator refuses door; demand single wicket match at Rectory: if narrator beats Grace, she considers his claims; Pearson on the Creed thrown.

**Ch XVII** – Team celebrates; champagne (Jennings, Miss Laura had two bottles); Rector's King Charles II bed; narrator tells Optimist.

**Ch XVIII** – Morning practice; Grace coaches bowling; narrator's bowling "putrid" (Biffin hit on head with bowling). Grace's bowling praised.

**Ch XIX** – Umpire dispute (Biffin); narrator concedes; Grace's splendid isolation. Single wicket match: Grace bats first? (narrator bats first; scores 23, caught by Optimist dropping).

**Ch XX** – Narrator's fielding; Grace scores; Grace declares by knocking own wicket with bat; Biffin "fair hout." Grace wins; narrator still bowls badly.

**Epilogue** – Morning Post: "DIMSDALE–TRENTHAM," 11th inst., Parish Church, Hickory, by Rev. E. J. H. Elphinstone, Richard Cranford Dimsdale to Laura Mary ("Grace") Trentham, daughter of Hon. Rev. George Trentham, D.D., Rector of St Mary's, Hickory.

**Footnotes:** Daily Chronicle on Optimist's tip; Oval "crowd" vs Lord's "company"; toss incident "art ought not to subscribe to the Press Association."
